title: Enabling Low Latency for ECQF based Flow Aggregation Scheduling in Time-Sensitive Networking
problem: Cyclic Queuing and Forwarding (CQF) with fixed cycle lengths on flow paths renders certain flows unschedulable. Enhanced CQF (ECQF) proposes variable cycle lengths as a conceptual solution but lacks concrete implementation details.
motivation: Time-Sensitive Networking applications require deterministic low-latency guarantees, which existing CQF mechanisms fail to provide for heterogeneous flow patterns.
method: JACO (Jointly Optimize aggregation Cycle and flows' Offsets) jointly optimizes aggregation cycle length and per-flow offset values to realize ECQF-based flow aggregation. An incremental heuristic algorithm is designed to solve the optimization problem efficiently. Performance is evaluated using OMNet++ simulation across diverse scenarios.
key_novelty: Joint optimization of aggregation cycle and flow offsets enables practical ECQF implementation with reduced latency and improved resource utilization.
contributions: JACO mechanism for implementing ECQF-based flow aggregation through joint cycle and offset optimization
Incremental heuristic algorithm for efficient JACO optimization
Simulation-based evaluation demonstrating latency reduction and improved resource utilization versus ECQF baseline
